Laura Bassi is a physicist. Laura Maria Caterina Bassi Veratti (29 October 1711 – 20 February 1778) was an Italian physicist and academic.
Who among these is a chemist?
Carolyn Bertozzi is a chemist. Carolyn Ruth Bertozzi (born October 10, 1966) is an American chemist and Nobel laureate, known for her wide-ranging work spanning both chemistry and biology.
What is the atomic number of Neon?
Neon is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ne and the atomic number 10.
In what year was Kitty Oppenheimer born?
Kitty Oppenheimer: Robert Oppenheimer, the director of the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos Laboratory during World War II.
In what year was Penicillin discovered?
Penicillin was discovered in 1928 by the Scottish physician Alexander Fleming as a crude extract of P. rubens.
In what year was Coulomb's law discovered?
Coulomb's law: This electric force is conventionally called the electrostatic force or Coulomb force.
Which company manufactures Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil?
Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil: Airbus Helicopters. The AS355 Ecureuil 2 is a twin-engine variant, marketed in North America as the TwinStar.
In which country is Junkers Ju 52?
Junkers Ju 52: Germany. Development of the Ju 52 commenced in the late 1920s, headed by German aeronautical engineer Ernst Zindel.
Who is credited with discovering Indium?
Indium: Ferdinand Reich. Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
Who is credited with discovering Californium?
Californium: Stanley Gerald Thompson. Californium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cf and atomic number 98.
Who is credited with discovering Fluorine?
Fluorine: Henri Moissan. Fluorine is a chemical element; it has symbol F and atomic number 9.
This is the most common genetic cause of dwarfism, typically producing short arms and legs with a normal-length torso and an enlarged head with a prominent forehead — what condition is it?
Achondroplasia is a genetic disorder whose primary feature is dwarfism.
With one stable isotope and the rank of 12th-most-abundant element in the universe, this lightweight metal carries atomic number 13 — what is it?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
The largest genus in the arum family with roughly 1,000 species, this flowering plant group is native to the Americas, ranging from northern Mexico down to northern Argentina — which genus?
Anthurium (Schott, 1829) is a genus of about 1,000 species of flowering plants, the largest genus of the arum family, Araceae.

Distinguished from celestial mechanics by asking what heavenly bodies ARE rather than where they are, this science applies physics and chemistry to the Sun, stars, galaxies, and exoplanets — which discipline?
Astrophysics is a science that applies the methods and principles of physics and chemistry in the study of astronomical objects and phenomena including the universe.
This perennial flowering plant species, native to Eurasia and growing up to four feet tall, includes cultivated varieties used for sugar, its edible root, and its edible leaves — what species is it?
Beta vulgaris (beet) is a species of flowering plant in the subfamily Betoideae of the family Amaranthaceae.

Developed in Germany from the Old English Bulldog and the now-extinct Bullenbeisser, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog breed is known for its square muzzle, underbite, and powerful bite — name the breed?
Boxer (dog breed) is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.
The leaves and buds of this evergreen shrub, when processed differently, yield green, black, oolong, white, and yellow varieties of the world's most popular hot beverage — what's the species?
Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
Taken by mouth with effects lasting about a day, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever, hives, and dermatitis with less drowsiness than older allergy medications — what is it?
Cetirizine is a second-generation peripherally selective antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), dermatitis, urticaria (hives), and runny nose.
Marked by a stopped heartbeat and halted breathing, this reversible-sounding medical state was given its name once CPR and defibrillation made post-arrest resuscitation possible — what's it called?
Clinical death is the medical term for cessation of blood circulation and breathing, the two criteria necessary to sustain the lives of human beings and of many other organisms.
Born in 1863, this Italian mathematician is remembered chiefly as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
Corrado Segre (20 August 1863 - 18 May 1924) was an Italian mathematician who is remembered today as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry.
This progressive, incurable neurocognitive syndrome — often tied to Alzheimer's — brings a decline in memory, thinking and motivation across mild-to-major stages. What is it?

Dementia is a syndrome, often associated with neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's, and characterized by a general decline in cognitive processes that affects the ability to perform everyday activities.
This unexplained skin condition produces itchy, fluid-filled blisters just millimeters wide on the palms, fingers, or soles, often clearing within a month only to recur — what is it?
Dyshidrosis is a type of dermatitis, characterized by itchy vesicles of 1-2 mm in size, on the palms of the hands, sides of fingers, or bottoms of the feet.
With a US prevalence of about 8.2 cases per million births, this inherited disorder can cause complications from esophageal narrowing to skin cancer to amputation — which condition?
Epidermolysis bullosa (EB) is a group of rare medical conditions that result in easy blistering of the skin and mucous membranes.

Named for a physicist who reportedly asked 'But where is everybody?' over lunch in 1950, this puzzle contrasts the vast odds of alien civilizations with our total lack of evidence for them — what's it called?
Fermi paradox is the term for the apparent gap between the lack of conclusive evidence of extraterrestrial civilizations and the apparently high likelihood of their existence.

Discovered in Paris in 1875 and bearing the symbol Ga on the periodic table, this soft, silvery chemical element has such a low melting point — just below 30°C — that it turns liquid at warm room temperature. Name this element?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
This term describes the overall system of processes, rules, and power structures that sets boundaries of conduct and steers the direction of an organized group — what is it?

Governance is the overall complex system or framework of processes, functions, structures, rules, laws and norms born out of the relationships, interactions, power dynamics and communication within an organized group of individuals.

His synergy with information-theory father Claude Shannon laid foundations for the Information Age, and during WWII he helped build automatic guns that defended London from V-1 flying bombs — who was this Dutch-American control-theory pioneer?
Hendrik Wade Bode (-d,; December 24, 1905 - June 21, 1982) was an American engineer, researcher, inventor, author and scientist, of Dutch ancestry.
Often caused by kidney failure or certain blood-pressure medications, this condition means too much potassium in the blood, with levels above 5.5 mmol/L — what's it called?
Hyperkalemia is an elevated level of potassium (K+) in the blood.
With the formula Fe2O3, this reddish inorganic compound occurs naturally as the mineral hematite, a key raw material for the steel industry — which compound?
Iron(III) oxide is the inorganic compound with the formula Fe2O3. It occurs in nature as the mineral hematite, which serves as the primary source of iron for the steel industry.
This Johns Hopkins psychologist coined the terms 'gender role' and 'sexual orientation' and believed gender was malleable during a child's first two years. Who was he?
John Money (8 July 1921 - 7 July 2006) was a New Zealand American psychologist, sexologist and professor at Johns Hopkins University known for his research on human sexual behavior and gender.
Endemic to New Zealand, this large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot has owl-like forward-facing eyes and holds the title of the world's only flightless parrot — what bird is it?
Kākāpō (Mori:; pl.: kkp; Strigops habroptilus), sometimes known as the owl-parrot, is a species of large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot of the superfamily Strigopoidea.
Popular in aquariums but a destructive invader in the Atlantic and Mediterranean, this venomous Indo-Pacific creature warns predators off with bold red and black stripes — what is it?
Lionfish (genus Pterois) are venomous marine fish native to the Indo-Pacific.
Domesticated in southern Mexico about 9,000 years ago from wild teosinte, this grain was grown by Native Americans alongside beans and squash in the 'Three Sisters' method — name the tall grass crop?
Maize (Zea mays), also known as corn, is a tall stout grass that produces cereal grain.
Triggered by falling progesterone, this monthly discharge from the uterine lining signals that pregnancy hasn't occurred and typically first arrives at "menarche" between ages 11 and 13 — what is it?
Menstruation (also known as a period, among other colloquial terms) is the regular discharge of blood and mucosal tissue from the inner lining of the uterus through the vagina.
This Nissin Food Products founder invented instant chicken ramen and went on to create the Top Ramen and Cup Noodles brands — who is he?

Momofuku Ando (March 5, 1910 - January 5, 2007), born Go Pek-Hok (Peh-e-j: G Pek-hok; Ti-l: Go Pik-hok), was a Taiwanese-born, ethnic Chinese, Japanese inventor and businessman who founded Nissin Food Products Co., Ltd.

Nicknamed for its terrifying rate of tissue destruction, this fast-spreading bacterial infection doesn't actually consume flesh — the bacteria instead release toxins that destroy it — what is this disease called?
Necrotizing fasciitis (NF), also known as flesh-eating disease or flesh-eating bacteria, is an infection that kills the body's soft tissue.
Despite the zebra-like stripes on its legs, this shy mammal of the northeastern Congo is actually the giraffe's only living cousin — and the sole other member of the family Giraffidae. What is it?
Okapi (Okapia johnstoni), also known as the forest giraffe, and zebra giraffe, is an artiodactyl mammal that is endemic to the northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo in central Africa.

This inflammation of the skin around the nail is often triggered by frequent hand washing or cuticle trauma like nail biting, and is treated with antibiotics or antifungals depending on the cause — what condition is it?
Paronychia is an inflammation of the skin around the nail, often due to bacteria or fungi.

Associated with the early 20th century, this philosophical movement tries to objectively describe subjective conscious experience exactly as it appears, without assuming anything about the outside world — which movement?
Phenomenology (philosophy) is a philosophical study and movement largely associated with the early 20th century that seeks to objectively investigate the nature of subjective, conscious experience.

It plays out everywhere from the clans of traditional societies up through modern governments, and its practitioners negotiate, make laws, and sometimes wage war; what is this activity of settling a society's affairs?
Politics is the activity of settling affairs in an organized society. Politics is usually concerned with resolving issues within a society via a government.
This noncontagious autoimmune condition leaves dry, scaly patches of skin and can flare at the exact spot of an injury — a quirk called the Koebner phenomenon; what is it?
Psoriasis is a long-lasting, noncontagious autoimmune disease characterized by patches of abnormal skin.

This condition, often triggered by crush injuries or extreme exercise, causes skeletal muscle to break down so rapidly that it can turn urine tea-colored and damage the kidneys — what condition is it?
Rhabdomyolysis (shortened as rhabdo) is a condition in which damaged skeletal muscle breaks down rapidly.
Contracted from contaminated food, this bacterial illness typically causes diarrhea, fever, and cramps within a day or two of exposure — what is it called?
Salmonellosis is a symptomatic infection caused by bacteria of the genus Salmonella.
Setting a world record for mental calculation at London's Imperial College in 1980, this self-taught Indian prodigy also wrote books on math, puzzles, and astrology — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi (4 November 1929 - 21 April 2013) was an Indian mental calculator, astrologer, and writer, popularly known as the "Human Computer".
This circular muscle normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage, relaxing only as physiological function requires — what is it called?
Sphincter is a circular muscle that normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage or orifice and relaxes as required by normal physiological functioning.
Encompassing domestic pigs and their ancestor the Eurasian wild boar, this genus within the even-toed ungulate family Suidae is native across Eurasia and Africa — which genus?

Sus (genus) is the genus of domestic and wild pigs, within the even-toed ungulate family Suidae. Sus includes domestic pigs (Sus domesticus) and their ancestor, the common Eurasian wild boar (Sus scrofa), along with various other species.
What common name covers a group of spike-leaved flowering plants — mostly in the daisy family — whose prickles evolved purely to ward off hungry herbivores?
Thistle is the common name of a group of flowering plants characterised by leaves with sharp spikes on the margins, mostly in the family Asteraceae.
Caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis and treated with the antibiotic streptomycin, this tick-borne illness also goes by an animal-related nickname — what is it?
Tularemia is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.

Commanding the first spaceflight to carry multiple crew members in 1964, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first human to die during a space mission when his capsule's parachute failed on reentry in 1967 — who was he?
Vladimir Komarov (16 March 1927 - 24 April 1967) was a Soviet test pilot, aerospace engineer, and cosmonaut.
Twice Egypt's Minister of Tourism and Antiquities, this archaeologist has dug across the Nile Delta, the Western Desert, and the Upper Nile Valley — who is he?
Zahi Hawass (born May 28, 1947) is an Egyptian archaeologist, Egyptologist, and former Minister of Tourism and Antiquities, a position he held twice.
Widespread across Europe and into East Asia, this venomous snake looms large in British folklore but rarely delivers a fatal bite — what reptile?
Adder: Species of venomous snake. Vipera berus, commonly known as the common European adder and the common European viper, is a species of venomous snake in the family Viperidae.
This Italian physicist built the first true electric battery in 1799 and discovered methane, disproving the idea that electricity could only come from living bodies — who is he?
Alessandro Volta: Italian chemist and physicist (1745–1827)
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this white crystalline salt is mildly acidic in solution and is used as both a fertilizer and food additive — which compound?
Ammonium chloride: Chemical compound. Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as [NH4]Cl.
This scientific practice of systematically measuring the human body has been used in paleoanthropology, historical living-standards research, and modern clothing design — what is it called?
Anthropometry: Measurement of the human individual.

This umbrella term for joint disease covers conditions like osteoarthritis, most common in weight-bearing joints as people age, and the autoimmune form that typically targets the hands and feet. What condition is this?
This Indian jurist studied economics at Columbia and the London School of Economics before becoming the chief architect of his country's constitution. Who was he?
B. R. Ambedkar: Indian jurist, economist, politician and social reformer (1891–1956)

This Swiss-American engineer was the only one of a famous physicist's three known biological grandsons to survive childhood, and later earned patents in electronics while working at Texas Instruments — who was he?

Developed to supplement the 727 on short routes, this narrow-body twinjet kept the 707's fuselage width and six-abreast seating and entered service with Lufthansa in 1968 — which best-selling aircraft is it?
A tree-like cluster of dark-green flower heads sprouting from a thick pale stalk, this cabbage-family vegetable is a close cousin of cauliflower and can be eaten raw or cooked — what is it?
Broccoli: Edible green plant in the cabbage family.
First synthesized in 1950 by bombarding curium with alpha particles, this actinide element bears the symbol Cf and is named for a US university and state — what is it?
Californium: Chemical element with atomic number 98 (Cf)
This corvid, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic, is stockier and larger than its North American cousin but nearly identical in appearance — what bird is it?
Carrion crow: Species of bird. The carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.
In a joint presentation with Alfred Russel Wallace, this English naturalist unveiled the idea that the struggle for existence drives a process he likened to selective breeding — who was he?
Charles Darwin: English naturalist and biologist (1809–1882)
This genus native to South and Southeast Asia gave rise to oranges, lemons, and limes through extensive hybridization — what is it?

Though its wild populations are considered vulnerable to extinction, this domesticated freshwater fish has been introduced so widely that it's listed among the world's 100 worst invasive species — what is it?
Common carp: Species of fish. It gives its name to the carp family, Cyprinidae.
Also nicknamed the prairie wolf, this adaptable North American canine fills a similar ecological niche to Eurasia's golden jackal and was first spotted in Panama in 2013 — what is it?
Coyote: Species of canine native to North America.

Affecting about half of all adults and often treated with antifungal cream, this common scalp condition causes flaking and mild itchiness but isn't actually caused by poor hygiene. What condition is it?
Dandruff: Skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.

Driven by a gradient in chemical potential, this stochastic process describes the net movement of particles from areas of higher to lower concentration and can even reverse direction in spinodal decomposition — what physical process is this?
Diffusion: Transport of dissolved species from the highest to the lowest concentration region.
Defined in humans as an adult height of four foot ten or shorter, this condition's most common form — accounting for about 70% of cases — is a genetic disorder called achondroplasia. What is it?
Dwarfism: Small size of an organism, caused by growth deficiency or genetic mutations.
This stage of development begins right after fertilization, progressing from a single-celled zygote through a ball of cells called a morula — what is it called?
Embryo: Multicellular diploid eukaryote in its earliest stage of development.
This white solid is prized for binding iron and calcium ions into water-soluble complexes — handy for dissolving scale — and goes by a four-letter acronym. What is it?
In this common vision condition, distant objects appear sharp but close-up objects blur because light focuses behind the retina instead of on it - what is it?
Farsightedness: Eye condition in which light is focused behind instead of on the retina.
Sold under the brand name Prozac, this SSRI treats depression, OCD and panic disorder, and is also prescribed off-label for premature ejaculation — what is it?
Fluoxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It is also approved for treatment of major depressive disorder in adolescents and children 8 years of age and over.
Tucked beneath the liver, this pear-shaped organ stores and concentrates bile before releasing it to aid fat digestion in the small intestine — which organ?
Gallbladder: Organ in humans and other vertebrates.
The tallest land animal alive and the largest ruminant on Earth, its closest living relative is the okapi — which long-necked African mammal is it?

This algebraic structure — a set paired with an operation that's associative, has an identity element, and gives every member an inverse — is exemplified by the integers under addition. What is it called?

Group (mathematics): Set with associative invertible operation. The concept of a group was elaborated for handling, in a unified way, many mathematical structures such as numbers, geometric shapes and polynomial roots.
About the size of a closed fist and enclosed in a protective sac called the pericardium, this four-chambered organ sits in the chest between the lungs and pumps blood through the body — which organ?
Heart: Organ found in humans and other animals.
Named for the English physician who first described it in 1832, this cancer is defined by multinucleated Reed–Sternberg cells in the lymph nodes — what is it?
Hodgkin lymphoma: Type of blood and immune-system cancer.
This immune response causes tissue damage upon repeated exposure to an antigen and underlies conditions like hay fever, which affects roughly one in ten people worldwide — what is it called?
Hypersensitivity: Overreaction of the immune system to an antigen.
This sugar alcohol, with about half the sweetness of table sugar, is made by the human kidney at roughly two grams a day and reaches its highest concentration in the brain — what is it?
Inositol: Carbocyclic sugar. Its formula is C6H12O6; the molecule has a ring of six carbon atoms, each with a hydrogen atom and a hydroxy group (–OH).
Often mislabeled 'yellowtail tuna' on sushi menus, this northwest Pacific jack fish is unrelated to true tuna and is called hamachi when served as sashimi — which species?
Japanese amberjack: Species of fish. The Japanese amberjack or yellowtail, Seriola quinqueradiata, is a species of jack fish in the family Carangidae, native to the northwest Pacific Ocean.
Also known as the English or Persian walnut, this tree species native to Eurasia is cultivated worldwide, with China as its leading producer today — what is it?
Juglans regia: Species of tree (walnut). Juglans regia, known by various common names including the common walnut, English walnut, or Persian walnut amongst other names, is a species of walnut.
Named from a Norwegian word for 'small fry of fish,' these shrimp-like crustaceans form a biomass of some 379 million tonnes in the Southern Ocean alone — which creatures?

Krill: Small, shrimp-like crustaceans; order of crustaceans. Krill (Euphausiids) (sing.: krill) are small and exclusively marine crustaceans of the order Euphausiacea, found in all of the world's oceans.
Spread by rats, dogs and other animals, this bacterial blood infection has an acute, jaundice-causing severe form known as Weil's disease — what's the condition?
Leptospirosis: Blood infection caused by bacteria.
Nicknamed the 'Dragon Lady,' this single-engine American spy plane flew covert missions above 70,000 feet over the Soviet Union, China, and Cuba from the 1950s — what is it?

This German physician and sexologist founded the Scientific-Humanitarian Committee, mounting what's been called the first advocacy for homosexual and transgender rights — and the Nazis revoked his citizenship in 1933. Who was he?
This German physicist won the 1914 Nobel for discovering how crystals diffract X-rays, then — a fierce opponent of Nazism — helped rebuild German science after the war. Who is he?
Originally known as amethopterin, this chemotherapy drug also treats autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and can end ectopic pregnancies — what is it?

Flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945 and code-named 'Zeke' by the Allies, this long-range carrier fighter combined agility, speed, and firepower unmatched early in WWII — which aircraft?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japanese carrier-based fighter aircraft. The A6M was designated as the Mitsubishi Navy Type 0 carrier fighter (零式艦上戦闘機, rei-shiki-kanjō-sentōki), or the Mitsubishi A6M Rei-sen.
Which condition describes a total absence of speech that can result from injury, illness, trauma, or a developmental or neurological disorder — sometimes only temporary?
Muteness: Medical condition. In human development, muteness or mutism is defined as an absence of speech, with or without an ability to hear the speech of others.
This medical term for a birthmark or mole covers marks present at birth as well as ones that appear later in life — what is it called?
Nevus: Mole or birthmark; visible, circumscribed, chronic skin lesion.
This medical condition, defined by a body mass index over 30, is linked to heart disease, type 2 diabetes and sleep apnea — what is it?
Obesity: Medical condition of excess body fat.
This fluid-filled sac that forms within the ovary is usually harmless and often tied to ovulation, appearing as a follicular or corpus luteum type — what is it?
Ovarian cyst: Fluid-filled sac in the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.
Best known for creating Gmail, this engineer also built the first prototype of Google's ad platform and once suggested the company's old motto, 'Don't be evil' — who is he?
Sold under the brand name Luminal, this WHO-recommended barbiturate treats epilepsy in children and can be given intravenously for status epilepticus — which drug?
Phenobarbital: Medication of the barbiturate type.
Injected by a mosquito's bite and multiplying first in the liver before invading red blood cells, this parasite genus is the cause of malaria — what is it?
Plasmodium: Genus of parasitic protists that can cause malaria.
Originating in Spain's Canary Islands, this large mastiff-type breed was historically used for guarding, herding sheep and cattle, and — legally until 1936 — dog fighting. Which breed?
Presa Canario: Spanish breed of dog. It originates in the Spanish autonomous community of the Canary Islands, and is found mostly in the islands of Gran Canaria and Tenerife.
Usually caused by E. coli spreading up the urinary tract, this kidney infection typically brings fever and flank tenderness, and can be prevented by urinating after sex — what condition is it?
Pyelonephritis: Inflammation of the kidney. It is typically due to a bacterial infection, most commonly Escherichia coli.
From a startled jump to a cat automatically reorienting itself mid-fall, this involuntary, split-second reaction runs through the nervous system without needing conscious thought — what's it called?
Reflex: Automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus.
Usually hidden underground, this plant organ anchors it in place while drawing in water and nutrients — what is it?
Root: Basal organ of a vascular plant.

With ears set low to detect prey moving underground and furry paw soles that insulate against scorching ground, this small desert feline was first described in the Algerian Sahara in 1858 — which animal?
Sand cat: Small wild cat species (Felis margarita)
Born in Moscow and brought to the US at age six, this computer scientist co-founded Google with Larry Page and served as president of its parent company until 2019 — who is he?
This big cat of the genus Panthera prowls the alpine zones of Central and South Asia at elevations of 3,000 to 4,500 meters, from the Himalayas to southern Siberia — what is it?
Snow leopard: Species of large felid.

First recognized as a distinct breed by the UK Kennel Club in 1935, this purebred originated in 19th-century Birmingham from crosses of bulldogs with various other breeds developed for close combat — what breed is it?
Staffordshire Bull Terrier: British breed of dog.

Blending geodesy, trigonometry, and law, this profession uses tools like theodolites, GNSS receivers, and lidar scanners to fix the exact positions of points on Earth for maps and property boundaries — what is it?
Surveying: Science of determining the positions of points and the distances and angles between them.

Found at the ends of linear chromosomes, this repetitive DNA region works with specialized proteins to prevent the chromosome tip from being mistaken for a damaging double-strand break — what is it called?
Telomere: Region of repetitive nucleotide sequences on chromosomes.
The largest cat of the genus Panthera, this Asian apex predator wears orange fur with mostly vertical black stripes and ranges from snowy Russian forests to tropical Indian jungles — what is it?
This chromosomal condition gives a female an extra sex chromosome beyond the usual pair, often producing no noticeable symptoms — fewer than 1 in 10 who have it even know. What is the condition?
Trisomy X: Chromosome disorder in women.
This Soviet chemist led efforts to contain the 1986 Chernobyl disaster and later briefed the international community in Vienna, though he omitted key design flaws in the reactor. Who was he?
Valery Legasov: Former Soviet inorganic chemist and member of the USSR Academy of Sciences (1936–1988)
In quantum mechanics, this idea captures how photons and electrons can act like discrete billiard-ball-like objects in some experiments and like spreading ripples in others — what is it?
Wave–particle duality: Concept in quantum mechanics. It expresses the inability of the classical concepts such as particle or wave to fully describe the behavior of quantum objects.
This Japanese media artist and academic directs a research centre for 'Digital Nature' and holds visiting professorships at multiple Japanese art universities — who is he?
Yoichi Ochiai: Japanese academic, artist, and entrepreneur. Yoichi Ochiai (落合 陽一, Yoichi Ochiai; born 16 September 1987) is a Japanese media artist, entrepreneur, and academic.
What is the chemical symbol for tin?
The symbol for tin is Sn. Tin is a chemical element; it has the symbol Sn and atomic number 50.
What is the chemical symbol for copernicium?
The symbol for copernicium is Cn. Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.

In what year was Richard Harris born?
Richard Harris: Richard St John Francis Harris (1 October 1930 – 25 October 2002) was an Irish actor and singer.
In what year was Jet Li born?
Jet Li Lianjie (courtesy name Yangzhong; born 26 April 1963) is a martial artist, actor, and philanthropist.
In what year was Melanie Griffith born?
Melanie Griffith: Melanie Richards Griffith (born August 9, 1957) is an American actress.
In what year was Sofia Coppola born?
Sofia Coppola: Sofia Carmina Coppola ( KOH-pə-lə; born May 14, 1971) is an American filmmaker and former actress.
In what year was Sharon Tate born?
Sharon Tate: Sharon Marie Tate Polanski (January 24, 1943 – August 9, 1969) was an American actress and model.
In what year was Taika Waititi born?
Taika Waititi: Taika David Cohen (born 16 August 1975), known professionally as Taika Waititi ( TY-kə WY-tee-tee), is a New Zealand filmmaker, writer, actor, and comedian.
In what year was Nicholas Hoult born?
Nicholas Hoult: Nicholas Caradoc Hoult (born 7 December 1989) is an English actor.
In what year was Charles Bronson born?
Charles Bronson (born Charles Dennis Buchinsky; November 3, 1921 – August 30, 2003) was an American actor.
In what year was Sage Stallone born?
Sage Stallone: Sage Moonblood Stallone (May 5, 1976 – July 13, 2012) was an American actor.
In what year was Rashida Jones born?
Rashida Jones: Rashida Leah Jones ( rə-SHEE-də; born February 25, 1976) is an American actress and filmmaker.
